title: Decolonisation: Empires End

cards.h: In 1945 empires ruled a third of humanity. By 1975 they were gone
cards.b:
When the UN was founded in 1945, it had 51 members. Today it has 193. Almost all the extra countries are former colonies.

In about thirty years, one of the biggest political changes in human history took place.
World War II had drained Britain and France. The US and USSR both pushed against old empires. Colonised people had also fought in the war and wanted freedom.

India's freedom came via mass non-violent movements and then talks. Vietnam beat France at Dien Bien Phu (1954) after a long war. In Algeria, a brutal war (1954-62) ended French rule. Ghana's Kwame Nkrumah won independence in 1957 through strikes and elections.

Britain used force against the Mau Mau in Kenya, with serious abuses.

Britain and France, with Israel, attacked Egypt to retake the Suez Canal. The US and USSR forced them to withdraw. It showed the old powers were no longer in charge.

In 1960 the UN General Assembly adopted Resolution 1514, declaring colonialism must end.

New states inherited borders that cut across peoples. Many faced coups, civil wars and poverty. Portugal held its colonies until 1974-75. Some historians call the continuing economic influence of ex-rulers 'neocolonialism' (a term of Nkrumah's, 1965).

Myth: empires handed power over politely.Fact: there were many wars: Algeria, Vietnam, Kenya, Angola, Indonesia. Even India's independence came with Partition, in which perhaps one to two million died (estimates vary) and about 15 million were displaced.

A tryst with destiny

At midnight on 14–15 August 1947 India became free, and Nehru gave his speech, Tryst with Destiny. Pakistan came into being a day earlier. India's freedom was the first big blow to the European empires in Asia.

Burma left the Empire in January 1948, Ceylon in February 1948 and Indonesia won independence in 1949. Nehru had hosted the Asian Relations Conference in Delhi in March 1947, and India led demands at the UN against colonial rule.

Freedom came with Partition, which killed hundreds of thousands of people and uprooted some 15 million. Decolonisation was never only a celebration.

Five things to remember

  1. The UN grew from 51 to far more members.
  2. Roads to freedom differed.
  3. Suez (1956) showed old powers' decline.
  4. Many new states faced hard borders.
  5. India helped lead the Afro-Asian cause.

Think about it

  • Why did colonial powers lose will?
  • Do old borders cause today's conflicts?
